Brown butter oat biscuits

These are the biscuits I make when there is nothing in the house, because there is always butter, and there are always oats at the back of the cupboard behind the things I bought for one recipe and never used again. They take ten minutes of work, one pan and no planning at all.

Ingredients

  • 150 g unsalted butter
  • 120 g soft brown sugar
  • Sea salt
  • 200 g rolled oats

Method

  1. Melt the butter in a wide pan and keep it on the heat until it smells of toasted nuts and the foam turns golden
  2. Take it off the heat at once, stir in the sugar and a good pinch of salt, and leave it for five minutes.
  3. Rest the dough
  4. Fold in the oats, press the mixture into a lined tin and bake at 170 degrees for twenty minutes, until the edges have darkened
  5. Cut into squares while still warm, then leave them in the tin until completely cold.

Tips

  • Use a pale pan so that you can see the colour of the butter change
  • Jumbo oats make a looser biscuit that breaks when you cut it, so save them for porridge.
  • The biscuits keep for a week in a tin and are better on the second day than on the first.
  • They freeze well, wrapped in pairs, for up to three months

Questions

Can I use salted butter instead?

Yes, and leave out the pinch of salt. The browning takes a little longer because salted butter holds more water.

Why did mine turn out greasy?

Almost always because the butter was still hot when the oats went in. Give it the full five minutes and they will soak it up instead of frying in it.

Glossary

Brown butter
Butter cooked gently until its milk solids toast and sink. The French call it hazelnut butter, after the smell, and it burns within seconds of being ready.
Rolled oats
Whole oat groats that have been steamed and flattened between rollers, which is why they cook in minutes while the cut kind takes half an hour.
